newsitem.title: FRANCE: KAL sees ex-Europe autumn cargo rate rise.
newsitem.headline: KAL sees ex-Europe autumn cargo rate rise.

text.p: Korean Airlines (KAL) said it was planning to increase ex-Europe rates by five to 10 percent to Korea and Japan during the autumn period.

"We have yet to make a firm decision on the scale of the rate increases and their date of application because of the reticence shown on the part of several of our European cargo stations to such a move," Denis Lemoin, KAL's Paris-based assistant cargo manager (Europe), told Reuters.
He said KAL's cargo stations in Amsterdam, Brussels, Basle and Frankfurt had expressed mixed feelings about the proposed increases because of the impact they might have on already strong competition.
"Nevertheless, we expect each of European stations to agree to the increases which will probably work out at five to 10 percent," Lemoin said.
KAL last adjusted ex-Europe rates in April 1996.
"Ex-Europe rates to destinations in South-East Asia, such as Hong Kong, Taipei, Bangkok and Singapore, would probably remain unchanged as we are not really competitively-priced in these markets."
If September proved to be a strong month, KAL would very likely implement the ex-Europe increases to Seoul and Japan in early October, and failing that, in November, Lemoin said.
"Our customers were notified some time ago that we were planning to increase our rates in the autumn so whenever we do implement them it will not come as a total surprise."
"Over the past three weeks, KAL had noted a slight recovery in the ex-Europe market but it was too early to say whether this marked a temporary upturn or something more durable.
"We are hoping for a strong finish to the year but the market has become very difficult to predict."
Lemoin added there was a strong chance KAL's current Boeing 747-200F programme from Europe would remain unchanged during the forthcoming winter season.
KAL operates 12 full-freighter flights from Europe to Seoul leaving from Frankfurt (four weekly), Paris (two), Basle (two), Amsterdam (one), London (one), Brussels (one) and Milan (one).
